title: Scheduling and Data Import Automation
keywords: cli tools, background jobs, and automation
learning_outcomes: Explain what scheduling and data import automation contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: periodic data synchronization.

content.intro: CLI scripts and background jobs need explicit inputs, predictable exit behavior, bounded resource use, observable failures, and safe retry semantics. Long-running work should not rely on a browser request staying open. In this lesson, focus on periodic data synchronization; then compare it with csv imports. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use scheduling and data import automation when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: CLI scripts and background jobs need explicit inputs, predictable exit behavior, bounded resource use, observable failures, and safe retry semantics. Long-running work should not rely on a browser request staying open. For scheduling and data import automation, begin with periodic data synchronization. Also distinguish csv imports; external api polling; batch processing. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
